**Finding: deviation (§ 19.2, paragraph p0076)**

The warranty architecture in Section 19 is largely sound and I did not flag it:

- **§ 19.1** — professional and workmanlike standard, qualified personnel, industry standards, plus material conformity to documentation and specifications (no stated duration).
- **§ 19.3** — no malicious code, compliance with Applicable Law, no functionality diminution, open-source protection for Customer source code.
- **§ 19.4** — the full preferred remedy ladder: prompt re-performance/repair/replace, then terminate and refund Fees paid, with carve-outs from exclusivity for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims.
- **§ 19.5** — the disclaimer is mutual and expressly does *not* limit express warranties, service levels, indemnities or stated remedies, so it does not swallow the express warranty.

**The one material failure is duration.** § 19.2 caps the Deliverable conformity warranty at fifteen days after delivery and then adds that Vendor "has no correction or refund obligation" afterwards — language that cuts off the otherwise untimed § 19.1 conformity warranty and the § 19.4 remedy. Two aggravating points:

1. Deliverables are defined in § 1.4 as custom work product (reports, configurations, integrations), so the services benchmark applies: 90 days preferred, 30 days fallback. Fifteen days sits below the fallback.
2. The window is effectively consumed by the fifteen-business-day acceptance test in § 6.1, so it expires at almost the same moment and leaves no coverage for defects surfacing in normal productive use.

**Redline (validated, ok:true):** extend "fifteen days" to "ninety (90) days" and confine the cut-off to Section 19.2 so it cannot override § 19.3, the service levels or the indemnities. Thirty days is flagged to the counterparty as an available fallback.
